title: Gas exchange in leaves and lungs
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:22Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-12T17:07:12Z recheck: the fresh check agreed with the fix, cleared with the fix

match.reason: The bank point covers only the human respiratory system, while the new point also covers gas exchange through stomata in leaves, which is a broader idea that the bank point does not teach.

draft.title: Gas exchange in leaves and lungs
card: take in carbon dioxide through tiny holes called stomata, mostly on the underside. Plants use it to make sugars.
take in oxygen through tiny air sacs called alveoli. The oxygen passes into the blood.
Both have a large surface for gases to cross. A leaf is flat and thin. The lungs hold millions of alveoli.
Both surfaces are also very thin, so gases only have a short distance to travel.
draft.remember: Stomata and alveoli let gases cross a large, thin surface.

a.q: Which pair correctly matches each organ with what it takes in?
opts: Leaf takes in carbon dioxide, lung takes in oxygen
Leaf takes in oxygen, lung takes in carbon dioxide
Leaf takes in carbon dioxide, lung takes in carbon dioxide
Leaf takes in oxygen, lung takes in oxygen
a.why: Leaves take in carbon dioxide through stomata, and lungs take in oxygen through alveoli. Swapping them is tempting because people often link plants with oxygen, but that is not what the leaf takes in here.
a.clue: Plants use a gas to make sugars.

b.q: Sam says a lung is good at gas exchange because it has millions of alveoli. Which feature of the lungs does this describe?
opts: A large surface for gases to cross
A very thin surface for gases to cross
A set of holes that open to the air
A flat shape that catches sunlight
b.why: Millions of tiny sacs add up to a very large surface. Thinness is a different feature, as it is about how far gases travel. Stomata are the holes in leaves, not alveoli.
b.clue: Many small sacs add up to how much area?

wants.brief: Two labelled diagrams: a leaf cross-section showing a stoma on the underside with carbon dioxide entering, and a cluster of alveoli with oxygen entering a blood vessel.
wants.why: It shows where gases cross in each organ.

a.best: Leaf takes in carbon dioxide, lung takes in oxygen

b.best: A large surface for gases to cross

problems.detail: Leaves also take in oxygen for respiration, especially at night, so 'Leaf takes in oxygen, lung takes in oxygen' is not strictly false. Wording such as 'for making sugars' or 'mainly takes in during the day' would make the intended answer the only right one.

check.summary: The card and answers are correct. One small issue: question a could tie the leaf's gas to making sugars, since leaves also take in some oxygen for respiration.
